existenceCheck.summary: Confirmed real. Announced April 2, 2025 in a Nintendo Direct alongside the Switch 2 console reveal. Released November 6, 2025, exclusively on Nintendo Switch 2. Developed by Koei Tecmo (AAA Games Studio), published by Nintendo (Koei Tecmo in Japan). Metacritic 79/100 (105 critic reviews), OpenCritic ~82%. Shipped over one million copies worldwide as of January 26, 2026. Director: Koki Aoyanagi.

findings.name: Mission-based campaign (not classic grid Adventure Mode, not open-world)
findings.detail: Wikipedia's gameplay description: 'The player controls 1 of up to 4 characters deployed to a given mission, where they must complete certain objectives while fighting off large groups of enemies.' No hub/base-camp, world map, or overworld-between-battles was described in the sources checked, but absence of a mention is not proof of absence. This reads as the mission-select structure used in recent Warriors titles (Age of Calamity-style discrete battle maps) rather than the original Hyrule Warriors' grid-based Adventure Mode or a fully open world.
findings.trackable: Unconfirmed — could not verify a mission list, completion checklist, or map screen.

findings.name: Two-player co-op
findings.detail: Local split-screen on one system, or cross-system via GameShare (only one player needs to own the game).

findings.name: Princess Zelda
findings.detail: Protagonist, time-travels to the Imprisoning War era; confirmed playable in trailers and store listing.

findings.name: King Rauru
findings.detail: Confirmed playable in trailers/store listing ('Princess Zelda, King Rauru, and other legendary heroes').

findings.name: Mineru
findings.detail: Listed among playable characters on the official Nintendo store page.

findings.name: Calamo (Korok wanderer)
findings.detail: Named as receiving a new Sync Strike paired with Zelda in a free post-launch update, implying an existing playable roster slot.

findings.name: Mysterious/Knight Construct
findings.detail: A construct powered by a Master Sword shard, styled after Link. Store listing references it gaining unlockable 'Unique Skills' via a free update, implying it is a playable unit.

findings.name: Queen Sonia
findings.detail: Major story character, Rauru's queen; killed by Ganondorf in the plot. Not explicitly confirmed as playable in any source checked — could be a story/NPC-only role.

findings.name: Tribal leaders: Raphica (Rito), Qia (Zora), Agraston (Goron), Ardi (Gerudo)
findings.detail: Named allied characters representing the four Hyrule tribes. Playable status not confirmed by any source checked — could be story allies only, or unlockable fighters (past Hyrule Warriors games have made similar tribal leader characters playable).

findings.name: Total playable character count
findings.detail: Could not find a confirmed final roster number for launch or post-update. Not stated in any source checked.

findings.name: Ganondorf
findings.detail: Main antagonist / final boss of the campaign, the Demon King.

findings.name: Grimgera
findings.detail: Described as 'one of four archfiends' — implies there may be a set of four archfiend-type bosses, but only Grimgera is named in sources checked.

findings.name: Phantom Ganon
findings.detail: Added as a new boss encounter via one of the two confirmed free post-launch content updates.

findings.name: Forbidden Difficulty
findings.detail: A new, harder difficulty mode unlocked via a free post-launch content update (not present at launch).
findings.trackable: Unconfirmed whether tracked/flagged anywhere in-game beyond difficulty selector.

findings.name: Replay Battles
findings.detail: Nintendo's product page mentions replaying story battles against more powerful enemies after completing the campaign ('The Howling Tempests' mission unlocks related bonuses).

findings.name: Weapon upgrade system via Zonaite Steel
findings.detail: Weapons are enhanced using a material called Zonaite Steel; a stronger variant, 'Pure Zonaite Steel,' was added via a free post-launch update for further upgrades.
findings.trackable: Unconfirmed whether a weapon-collection or upgrade-completion screen exists.

findings.name: Three additional weapons (free update)
findings.detail: Three new weapons were added as part of the free post-launch content updates; exact names not confirmed.

findings.name: Save-data crossover weapons
findings.detail: High Guard's Claymore unlocks from detecting Hyrule Warriors: Age of Calamity save data on the system; High Guard's Sword unlocks from detecting The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom save data. These appear to be one-time unlock bonuses rather than an ongoing collectible category.
findings.trackable: Unconfirmed how/where these are surfaced to the player (likely an item/weapon inventory).

findings.name: amiibo support
findings.detail: Scanning any compatible amiibo accessory grants in-game rewards including crafting materials and other items. Specific amiibo list and reward table not confirmed.
findings.trackable: Unconfirmed whether an amiibo-reward log exists in-game.

findings.name: Character upgrades via 'spoils'/resources
findings.detail: Outside missions, players spend collected resources (spoils) to upgrade characters, described in the Wikipedia gameplay summary as done 'with community assistance' (likely referencing NPC allies/sages), separate from weapon upgrades.
findings.trackable: Unconfirmed whether a per-character upgrade-completion tracker exists.

findings.name: No paid Expansion Pass confirmed
findings.detail: Only two FREE post-launch content updates were found (adding extra battles, Phantom Ganon boss, Forbidden Difficulty, 3 weapons, a new Sync Strike, Unique Skills for the Mysterious Construct, and Pure Zonaite Steel). No evidence of a paid Expansion Pass / Season Pass was found in any source checked, unlike some prior Hyrule Warriors titles. This could reflect genuine absence of paid DLC, or simply a gap in available search results given how recent the game is.

trackableStats.stat: Unknown — no in-game completion percentage, bestiary, weapon-collection screen, or mission checklist could be confirmed from available sources.

versionNotes.note: Game is Nintendo Switch 2 exclusive; no other platform release exists to compare against, so no cross-platform version differences apply.

Save-data bonus weapons (High Guard's Claymore, High Guard's Sword) depend on the player also owning/having played Hyrule Warriors: Age of Calamity and/or Tears of the Kingdom on the same Switch/Switch 2 system — a cross-save-dependent unlock, not universally available to all players.
